thread:
laura: quick heads-up — after the otel-collector rollout in prod we're losing trace_id in a subset of background worker logs (kafka consumers). dashboards can't link traces -> logs for those flows. anyone seen this pattern?
kevin: hmm — is the worker using the otel SDK + contextpropagation? background jobs often drop the context if we don't explicitly propagate.
priya: we switched the collector to span-only batch export (to reduce cost). logs still forwarded via filebeat -> es. could be we never inject the trace id into the JSON log payload.
sam: +1 on missing injection. also check sampling: if traces are dropped upstream sampling-wise, there won't be a matching trace, even if trace_id is present in logs. dashboards need the trace_id in logs to do link-joins.
laura: sample case: request comes in -> route -> enqueues job with headers, worker reads headers but our structlog JSON formatter doesn't read x-cloud-trace or otel baggage. example from worker:```
logger.info(json.dumps({"msg":"started job", "job_id": jid}))
```
kevin: we should add a small shim that pulls trace context from OTEL and injects trace/span ids into the log record. in python it looks like:```
from opentelemetry.trace import get_current_span
span = get_current_span()
ctx = span.get_span_context()
trace_hex = format(ctx.trace_id, '032x')
logger = structlog.get_logger()
logger = logger.bind(trace_id=trace_hex)
logger.info("job started", job=jid)
```
priya: for JVM services we added a Logback MDC enricher that reads `io.opentelemetry.context` and sets `trace_id`/`span_id` in the MDC. same idea for workers.
sam: two sticky/UX things for console: 1) treat trace_id as a first-class field in the logs index (not analyzed), and 2) when a trace view is open, show a quick faceted query that finds logs with trace_id OR request_id within +/- 5s. makes linking resilient when trace sampling differs.
laura: question on retention/cost: we can't keep full-trace retention forever. some traces are huge. any recs for retention + linking?
priya: we use tail-sampling in the collector: store a short span buffer in redis for 30s, decide which traces to keep, export sampled traces to expensive backend (honeycomb/jaeger) and always export trace_id to logs. logs have long retention; traces short. that way console can still join to logs even if the full span wasn't exported.
kevin: key implementation detail: make sure trace_id is deterministic format across systems (hex lowercase 32 chars). otherwise joins fail. also avoid storing high-cardinality fields like user_email on the span->logs join index.
infra-bot: deploy 1780c3 scheduled: otel-collector config v2 -> add `resource_attributes` and `log_injection` toggle.
laura: follow-up: for async flows that truly start without incoming span (cron jobs), create a new root span but still set trace_id on logs so the console link from metrics/time-series works.
sam: another edge case: cross-tenant routing. if tenant id is in headers, include `tenant_id` as resource attribute and also as a top-level log field, but keep it low-cardinality in the primary index (tokenized field elsewhere).
priya: plan action items: 1) small change in worker runtime to auto-inject trace_id/span_id when OTEL context present (PR in next sprint), 2) adjust log indexing mapping to store trace_id as keyword, 3) console UX: add fallback "Find related logs" that queries trace_id OR request_id +/- window.
laura: thanks, i'll draft the PR for worker shim and open a docs todo for the console fallback. cc @sam for index mapping changes.
kevin: FYI we should document exporter behavior: OTLP/gRPC keeps the full trace context best, jaeger/thrift sometimes flips ids. test exporter matrix.
laura: sounds good — will add tests that simulate sampled vs unsampled traces and ensure logs still have trace_id. :thumbsup:
